comments.text:
Mark, really I am not impressed with this Video. You say and show a side of Afghanistan that looks beautiful and tastes good. But what about the girls and women?
Under Taliban rule, women and girls in Afghanistan are systematically banned from public life and stripped of their fundamental human rights. Girls are prohibited from attending school past the sixth grade, and women are entirely barred from higher education and almost all forms of employment. In public spaces, women must be completely veiled, are not allowed to visit parks or gyms, and cannot travel without being accompanied by a close male relative. Furthermore, extreme restrictions prevent women from making their voices heard outside the home or accessing healthcare and justice independently. According to reports by UN Women and Human Rights Watch, these institutionalized restrictions effectively place half of the country's population under complete gender-based exclusion.
